title: Null-sentinel migration
blurb: Evaluates eight worker handler patterns against the real browser-fired connect event inside a SharedWorker to show which expressions flip branch when e.data changes from null to "".
question: Which real-world SharedWorker connect handler checks break when Chrome 160 changes MessageEvent.data from null to "", and which remain stable across Chrome 159 and 160?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153, 8/8 real-event expressions matched the legacy null column; 6 patterns (=== null, == null, ??, typeof === "object", JSON.stringify, String) change result between null and "", while !e.data and e.type === "connect" stay stable. Chrome 160 branch not verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 (legacy null branch verified); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Shared handlers using e.data === null, e.data == null, e.data ?? fallback, or typeof e.data === "object" flip branch in Chrome 160
friction.repro: Share one listener between connect and message events and test e.data === null or e.data ?? "default"; in Chrome 160+, e.data is "" (typeof "string"), so nullish checks no longer trigger.
friction.workaround: Branch on e.type === "connect" and adopt e.ports[0] (or e.source) instead of inspecting e.data.
